newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest wheat futures rebound on Chicago.
newsitem.headline: Budapest wheat futures rebound on Chicago.

text.p: Rising Chicago prices triggered a limit-up move by wheat futures on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE), traders said on Tuesday.
"Wheat prices were bound to go higher, the only question was the size of the increase," said Istvan Grebats of Termin.
He added that wheat futures were likely to continue to follow international markets in the absence of domestic information to trade on.
Milling wheat prices, after three days of downward movements, went higher for most maturities by the 400-forint limit, with only the March 1998 maturity falling to 25,300 forints, down 800.
May milling wheat finished at 24,900 forints, July at 21,400 and August at 21,960, all up 400 forints.
Maize prices remained steady for all but May and July.
May rose 100 forints to 18,600 on what Grebats said was the continued closing of speculative positions.
But he added that a correction could start any time as producers were likely to find these prices attractive enough to start selling excess stocks.
July maize finished 90 forints lower at 17,810 forints in relatively low turnover.
Feed wheat and feed barley prices rose as they followed milling wheat prices while sunflower attracted no business and was unchanged.
Total grains turnover rose slightly to 308 million forints or 685 contracts from Monday's 279.7 million forints.
